punchline: Lynch's first stock education was carrying golf bags for men who talked about stocks.
thirty_sec: Peter Lynch started caddying at eleven near Boston, carrying clubs for executives who talked about stocks. He followed those stocks in the paper, put a thousand dollars into an air-cargo company called Flying Tiger, and saw it rise tenfold. In 1966 about 75 people wanted three summer jobs at Fidelity, and he was the one who had caddied for its president for years. He got the job, and eleven years later he was running Magellan.
